thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 Alert: GeoDNS anomalies detected. Multiple customers in eu-west-1 are resolving geo.redwood.ai to our us-east-1 origin intermittently, causing cross-region spikes and elevated latency + some 502 errors. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geodns-failover

dinesh.p: ack. Im taking lead. First step: confirm resolver answer divergence across public resolvers and our authoritative clusters.

olivia.r: collecting traces now. Quick dig outputs:
```
$ dig +short geo.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
104.18.30.20

$ dig +short geo.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
34.200.120.5

$ dig +short geo.redwood.ai @ns-1.route53.redwood.com
34.200.120.5

$ curl -I --resolve geo.redwood.ai:443:104.18.30.20 https://geo.redwood.ai/health
HTTP/2 200

$ curl -I --resolve geo.redwood.ai:443:34.200.120.5 https://geo.redwood.ai/health
HTTP/2 200
```

olivia.r: looks like 1.1.1.1 is returning a Cloudflare edge IP (104.18.30.20) for some clients, while Route53 authoritative points to us-east public origin 34.200.120.5. That mismatch indicates Cloudflare cache/resolver skew or stale records in CF DNS layer.

sam.t: customer symptoms: eu-west customers see 1500-3000ms p95, and about 4% 502s. Our eu-west capacity is fine; the traffic is being routed to us-east due to resolved answers. We're seeing session affinity mismatches causing auth failures and retries.

dinesh.p: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily adjust GeoDNS policy to enforce regional pinning for eu-west -> set prefer-eu regions with strong health gating, 2) increase eu-west capacity by adding one extra hostpool as safety, 3) open immediate Cloudflare case with EDNS+TTL evidence, 4) notify customers.

netops-bot: action: scaled up eu-west hostpool +1 (2 -> 3) at 2026-03-16T03:12:05Z by dinesh.p

dinesh.p: flipping geo policy to prefer eu-west answers and set Cloudflare weight to 0 for traffic originating from EU/UK ASNs. Applying change now; will monitor for propagation.

incident-bot: action executed: GeoDNS policy "regional-pin-eu" updated: eu-west weight 100, cloudflare-weight 0 at 2026-03-16T03:13:22Z by dinesh.p

olivia.r: after flipping policy: partial improvement — p95 dropped ~40% but still seeing intermittent 5xx from clients hitting Cloudflare edges. Dig now shows mix still for some resolvers (1.1.1.1 returning CF IPs for certain edns-client-subnet ranges).

sam.t: sample edns: some upstream resolvers are using EDNS client-subnet that points to an ISP in the US, causing CF to return nearby US edge IPs. We may need to request Cloudflare to bypass client-subnet or adjust TTL/steering.

cloudflare-bot: Case created: CF-INC-543210. Assigned to L2 engineer. Provided dig traces, EDNS-client-subnet headers, resolver probe logs, and sample client IPs.

rebecca: Product impact: 18 paid tenants reported degraded performance; two opened support tickets flagged as Sev2. Support team has rapid FAQ ready. Drafting status message: "Partial geo-routing issue affecting some EU customers; mitigation enacted".

dinesh.p: additional mitigation: enable short-circuit health checks on our authoritative Route53 to return localized answers for queries with no EDNS CS, and add a sanity-check that compares authoritative answers to top-level public resolvers every 30s. sam, can you add that probe?

sam.t: on it. Adding cross-resolver comparator probe and an alert when >3% of queries differ for >60s.

olivia.r: note: lowering TTL on the Route53 records from 300s -> 60s to speed up steering changes. Doing this now.

netops-bot: action executed: route53 record ttl updated geo.redwood.ai 300 -> 60 at 2026-03-16T03:21:10Z by olivia.r

dinesh.p: handoff: I need to leave in 40m. Oliva, Maya please take on next watch. Keep CF fallback disabled until they confirm stable and EDNS behaviour normalized. If CF confirms a cache purge required, request they flush affected edge zones.

olivia.r: ack. Ill monitor CF case and our comparator probe. Will also prepare a short customer-facing timeline for the status page.

incident-bot: mitigation summary: regional pinning applied, eu-west capacity scaled, TTL lowered, cross-resolver probe enabled. Continued monitoring at 15s cadence.

rebecca: comms note: include "No customer data exposure suspected. Root cause under investigation with Cloudflare; remediation may require edge cache invalidation and EDNS config updates."

cloudflare-bot: Update from CF L2: "We see EDNS-client-subnet influencing edge selection in some POPs; will attempt targeted cache purge and evaluate bypassing client-subnet for our zone. ETA next update in 30-45m."

olivia.r: next actions and post-incident items for the postmortem: 1) automated detection for answer divergence across resolvers, 2) consider minimizing use of client-subnet-dependent edges or add geo-override for critical control plane endpoints, 3) test runbook for TTL/weight flips to avoid auth token mismatches, 4) customer rollback playbook.

rebecca: prepping postmortem and customer follow-up. Sam/Olivia to provide logs and timeline. Dinesh, please confirm any capacity cost changes for billing note.

dinesh.p: will surface cost delta. handoff to olivia.r at 2026-03-16T03:48:00Z.

(reacts: :eyes: from rebecca, :thumbsup: from sam.t)
